title: Line B up the right way
starter:
%Ab = buffer 4 dtype=f32 slot=0
%Bb = buffer 4 dtype=f32 slot=1
%Cb = buffer 4 dtype=f32 slot=2
%A  = load %Ab
%B  = load %Bb
%a3 = reshape %A [2 2 1]
%aT = permute %a3 [1 0 2]
%ax = expand %aT [2 2 2]
%b3 = reshape %B [2 2 1]
%bx = expand %b3 [2 2 2]
%p  = mul %ax %bx
%c  = reduce %p op=add pop=1
%cf = reshape %c [4]
%s  = store %Cb %cf
%C1 = after %Cb %s
hints: B is K x N. Which of the three axes k, m, n does B not have? That is where its size-1 axis goes.
The cube's axes are k, m, n. B has k and n, so it needs a 1 in the middle, where m is.
Change B's reshape to `[2 1 2]`. Then `expand` repeats row k of B down the m axis.
explain: B has a k axis and an n axis and no m axis, so its size-1 axis sits in the middle: `[2 1 2]`. With `[2 2 1]` the cube has the right shape and the wrong numbers, because B gets read as if its columns were m.
